lead.headline: Championship Thunder Shakes the Old Barn
lead.dek: A test-only issue stretches every column without pretending to report a real game.
body: This clearly labeled validation copy is deliberately long. It exists to make the renderer prove that dense editorial prose remains readable, balanced, and safely contained inside the newspaper grid.

Names, figures, scores, and circumstances in this fixture are fictional. The production edition must be supplied from the reconciled fact pack and will use the same renderer without a parallel layout.

The visual system borrows the authority of a local sports broadsheet: thick rules, narrow copy, emphatic headlines, restrained red accents, and a recurring folio that makes every page feel like one edition.

games.headline: A Twelve Goal Avalanche Buries the Visitors
body: The first test report uses enough prose to exercise the two-column game grid. It reports only fixture facts and makes no claim about a real league or a real player.
Long team names should wrap instead of colliding with the score, while the contributor list stays compact and legible beneath the report.

body: The second fixture creates a tighter scoreline and tests punctuation. Text such as <script>alert('never')</script> must appear as harmless text rather than executable markup.
This report also confirms that a game can have a short contributor list without leaving the rest of the page looking unfinished.
